subject: Discovery recap: FinHealth Private VPC requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Amit Rao <amit@finhealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 18:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: FinHealth Private VPC requirements

Thanks again for taking the time today, Amit — great conversation. Below is a short recap to make sure we captured your requirements and next steps. Please reply with any corrections or additions.

Key pain points and drivers
- Regulated workloads (financial + healthcare data) — strict data residency and audit requirements.
- Current vendor-hosted models have unacceptable egress & logging controls for sensitive PII.
- Need predictable latency for customer-facing features (sub-200ms target for short prompts).
- Concerned about vendor access to unencrypted data and key control.

Current stack / constraints
- Primary infra: AWS (us-east-1), VPCs with strict egress controls and no public inbound access.
- KMS: Customer-managed keys (CMKs) via AWS KMS; some workloads require HSM-backed keys.
- Identity: Okta SAML SSO, internal SCIM provisioning.
- Network: Firewall rules only allow outbound HTTPS through a proxy; some environments are air-gapped/testnets.

Success criteria for any POC / pilot
- Private control plane with no Redwood access to unencrypted data (customer-managed keys).
- Deployment inside a customer VPC or dedicated on-prem setup that meets your network constraints.
- Audit logging (immutable) and exportable logs for compliance reviews.
- Performance: 95th percentile token latency within your stated SLOs; support for batching and autoscaling.

Open questions we flagged
- Which environments require full air-gapped/offline operation vs. VPC-with-internet-restricted?
- Expected peak QPS and typical token length (so we can size a Dedicated pool for the POC).
- Legal/security contacts for SOC2 evidence access and questionnaire.

Next steps
1) I will share a short architecture sketch and a SOC2 snapshot (attached).
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra/security folks — proposed times next week (Mon/Tue morning ET).
3) You to confirm which environment(s) need air-gap and provide rough QPS numbers.

Attachments: SOC2-Type2-2025.pdf, redwood-private-vpc-architecture.pdf

Thanks — excited to see if we can get a secure POC running quickly.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123

From: Amit Rao <amit@finhealth.com>

Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 20:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: FinHealth Private VPC requirements

Thanks Marissa — this looks right and very helpful. A few clarifications:
- Air-gap: production payment pipelines must be air-gapped in our isolated DR region; dev/staging can use VPC with tightly controlled egress.
- QPS: For the initial pilot we expect ~50 QPS with 512-token average (user-facing routing). Peak could be ~200 QPS for a week of load testing.
- Security: Please route SOC2 and questionnaire to myself and Samantha Lee (cc) — Samantha handles vendor security reviews.

Next for us: Samantha will coordinate on a time for the technical deep-dive — prefer Tue 11am ET. Also will share the vendor security questionnaire (DOCX).

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—
Amit Rao
Director, Platform Engineering | FinHealth
amit@finhealth.com
